subject: SaltBay deployment synthesis — SLOs, model choices & next milestones
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ami Das <ami@saltbay.io>
Cc: Luis Moreno <luis.m@saltbay.io>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: SaltBay discovery recap: latency/throughput targets and next steps

Hi Ami / Luis —

Thanks again for the chat earlier — helpful to map the end-to-end flow. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the procurement conversation: 

Key pain / goals we captured:
- Current in-house ML infra cannot meet P99 latency for live support suggestions during peak traffic (customer-facing chat).
- SaltBay needs predictable per-request costs and clear fallbacks for degraded capacity.
- Data residency: core inference must run inside SaltBay VPC (HIPAA-ish workloads for some customers).

Agreed SLO targets (rough, for validation):
- P50 latency target: <= 40 ms per token (edge request path)
- P95 latency target: <= 80 ms per token
- P99 tail: <= 120 ms (hard constraint for UI snappiness)
- Sustained throughput target: 100–150 requests/sec for the primary model profile (peak bursts up to 320 rps with burst pool)

Model and quality constraints:
- Primary model family: open 13B-class (we discussed Llama-2-13B-like performance) with preference for INT8 quantized variants to hit cost targets.
- Some endpoints require deterministic output for reranking; we'll propose model pinning and eval guardrails.

Deployment topology we recommended:
1) Private (VPC) deployment for production inference with dedicated GPU pool (customer-managed networking).
2) Autoscale policy: baseline reserved capacity for 120 rps + burst pool (shared hosted capacity) up to 320 rps.
3) Smart routing: route premium customers to dedicated nodes; fallback to hosted compatible variant on capacity pressure.
4) KV/prefix cache for short-session reuse (saves ~25–40% token cost for chat flows).

Immediate next steps (action items):
- Neha: share mutual action plan (MPA) + rough SLO cost estimates (attached).
- Ami: confirm compliance checklist items SaltBay requires (KMS, SOC2 evidence).
- Luis: procurement will review MPA and indicate preferred contracting cadence.
- Karthik/Rishi: flag any early technical blockers by EOD Friday so we can scope a short lab POC.

Attachments: saltbay-mpa-draft.xlsx (MPA template), slo_estimates_saltbay.pdf (ballpark cost/latency tradeoffs).

Thanks — I’ll loop Karthik & Rishi into the next message for tech clarifications.

—Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0198

From: Ami Das <ami@saltbay.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Luis Moreno <luis.m@saltbay.io>, Procurement <procurement@saltbay.io>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 17:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SaltBay discovery recap: latency/throughput targets and next steps

Neha —

Appreciate the concise recap. Correct on the pain areas and SLOs look reasonable as a starting point. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The UI expects sub-150ms end-to-end for the full suggestion pipeline (that includes a ~20ms network hop to our front-end). Your P99 <=120ms requirement is tight but acceptable if the model execution itself is within ~90–95ms.
- For data residency: we can host the inference inside our AWS account (VPC). We will need to see KMS integration + an SOC2 report.
- On model determinism: our reranker must be replayable; if Redwood offers model pinning + eval hooks, that satisfies the ask.

Procurement (cc’d) — we’ll review the MPA; we typically negotiate term/commit over 30–45 days and will push back on multi-year lock-ins.

I’ll coordinate with Procurement on the compliance checklist and loop back next week.

—Ami
Director of Product, SaltBay Analytics
ami@saltbay.io

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ami Das <ami@saltbay.io>
Cc: Luis Moreno <luis.m@saltbay.io>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 18:03:00 -0800
Subject: Technical follow-up: perf knobs, KV cache and quantization recommendation

Karthik / Rishi — looping you in to confirm the technical approach and flag blocking questions.

Short notes for the POC we proposed: 
- Recommended model: 13B open family quantized to INT8 (tradeoff: ~12–20% relative quality regression vs FP16 but ~2.5–3x lower memory + lower latency).
- Kernel & runtime knobs: continuous batching with dynamic batch cap of 8 tokens / request for chat; prefer request-level batching for user-facing latency.
- KV cache: enable prefix-based KV caching for active sessions (TTL ~30s) — expect 25–40% token cost reduction on chat flows with 70% reuse.
- Latency packing: optimize sequence-length bucketing; aim to keep CNN attention kernels for short-context optimization.

Blocking questions for SaltBay (Ami):
1) Typical input length distribution (tokens): mean, 75th, 95th percentiles for user messages and overall sequence length.
2) Expected concurrent unique sessions during peak (guesstimate).
3) Any regulatory constraints requiring on-prem air-gapped options vs VPC in cloud?

If we can get the distributions I’ll produce a small sizing matrix (GPUs, expected P99 under different batch windows) and a simple canary plan: 1-week staged canary in VPC -> measure p99 for 7 days -> scale to baseline pool.

Attaching the MPA + cost/latency sketch again.

—Neha

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ami Das <ami@saltbay.io>
Cc: Luis Moreno <luis.m@saltbay.io>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Technical follow-up: perf knobs, KV cache and quantization recommendation

Thanks — quick technical commitments from our side to unblock procurement/POC scoping: 

1) Validation matrix: we will run a 48–72 hour lab test (our infra) with a representative token distribution you provide. Deliverables: observed latency distribution (P50/P95/P99), throughput vs tail-latency curves, and memory footprint for the selected INT8 variant.

2) Canary plan (VPC):
   - Phase A (Day 0–3): single model variant on 2x A10-equivalent GPUs, 0.5x predicted baseline traffic (smoke + correctness).
   - Phase B (Day 4–10): scale to baseline reserved pool (120 rps sustained) + enable KV cache; measure cost delta and real P99.
   - Phase C (post-Day 10): enable burst policy into hosted fallback for up to 320 rps and confirm graceful degradation.

3) Fallback mechanics: if P99 > 140ms during burst, Redwood will automatically route non-premium traffic to a lighter-weight hosted variant (same API, different model). Premium traffic retains dedicated capacity.

4) Security/compliance: we can support KMS integrations and will provide SOC2 artifact copies under an NDA; full air-gap is treated as a Professional Services engagement (timeline + cost TBD).

Action items from tech:
- Ami: token distribution + concurrent session estimate (see Neha’s questions).
- Neha: finalize MPA deliverable and hand to Procurement.
- Rishi: draft POC lab schedule and expected infra cost (Rishi will attach).

I’ll prepare the lab test plan and share by Monday morning.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
